## Fullscreen Mode

The `fullscreen: true` option captures the entire visible terminal grid,
like taking a screenshot. This is useful for TUI applications.

### System Processes (top)

Launch `top` and capture a snapshot of the screen:

```{term}
#| fullscreen: true
top -l 1 -n 5 #! hold: 2.0, expect_prompt: false
q #! literal: false, hold: 0.5, expect_prompt: true
```

### Directory Listing as Table

Create some files and show them:

```{term}
mkdir -p /tmp/term-demo
touch /tmp/term-demo/file{1..5}.txt
echo "hello" > /tmp/term-demo/file1.txt
echo "world" > /tmp/term-demo/file2.txt
ls -la /tmp/term-demo/
```

### Cleanup

```{term}
rm -rf /tmp/term-demo
```
